purpose: Venlafaxine is used to treat depression, anxiety, panic disorder, and social anxiety disorder. It can help lift your mood, reduce feelings of worry or fear, and improve your overall quality of life. Some doctors also prescribe it for nerve pain or hot flashes.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called serotonin and norepinephrine to help regulate mood and emotions. Venlafaxine works by keeping more of these chemicals available in your brain for longer. This helps improve communication between brain cells, which can lift your mood and reduce anxiety over time.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, dizziness, dry mouth, sweating, trouble sleeping, constipation, and decreased appetite are common, especially when you first start the medication. You may also notice increased blood pressure or a faster heart rate. Most side effects improve after the first few weeks as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms like dizziness, irritability, and flu-like feelings. It may increase suicidal thoughts in children, teens, and young adults, especially early in treatment, so watch for mood changes and contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication, and tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially MAOIs, as combining them can be dangerous.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 37.5 mg to 75 mg once daily, typically taken with food. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to 225 mg per day depending on how you respond. The extended-release (XR) form is taken once a day, while the regular form may be taken two or three times a day.
